basics.name: Luca Valentini
basics.label: Senior Unity Developer, Systems & Tools Programmer
basics.summary: Senior Unity Developer with 6+ years in Unity and C#, in studio teams since 2023. I build structured, self-contained game systems and the custom editor tooling that makes the whole team faster, backed by measured performance work on mobile.

work.name: KYKUYO
work.summary: Worked on SOLAR, a live free-to-play geolocation/AR mobile game on Google Play and the App Store.
highlights: Owned the character dressing system end-to-end: a node-graph garment system with backend sync and 8 authoring tools.
Built the NPC GPU rendering pipeline: 10 to 200 fps measured on device with a full NPC crowd.
Designed the camera context system, with the layer boundary enforced by the compiler.
Took the technical direction of SPCA x SOLAR across a 9-person team.
Shipped the onboarding flow, the in-app purchase store and the HUD.
Built internal editor tooling used across the team: 9 of the project's 35 custom editor tools.

work.name: Escuela Da Vinci
work.summary: Professor of Artificial Intelligence and pathfinding algorithms (2026 to present). Teaching Assistant in Programming for Thesis (2025).
highlights: Teaches Artificial Intelligence and pathfinding algorithms.
Helped students plan and architect the systems behind their thesis projects.

work.name: 3AM Games Studio
work.summary: Indie project alongside full-time work. Technical direction of Waxy: The Wick and the Witch, over 26 months in a 5-person team.
highlights: Wrote 10 of the project's 14 custom editor tools.
Led a full rework of the core mechanic, which got the project selected for the ADVA MPVP mentorship program.
Designed the wax and fire-state mechanics and the camera system.

work.name: Huawei Technologies
highlights: Handled 300 to 400 support tickets a month against an under-18-hour response-time SLA.
Kept a user satisfaction rating of 4.5/5 or higher.

projects.name: SOLAR
highlights: Owned the dressing system, the camera-context architecture and the NPC GPU rendering pipeline (10 to 200 fps on device).

projects.name: Waxy: The Wick and the Witch
projects.description: 3D puzzle-platformer by 3AM Games Studio. Wax is your health, your height as you melt, and the reach of your flame. Fully playable on a gamepad, menus included.
highlights: Led the rework of the core mechanic that got the project selected for the ADVA MPVP mentorship program; wrote 10 of its 14 custom editor tools.

projects.name: Snackdown
projects.description: 2D last-player-standing multiplayer platformer, server-authoritative, with hand-written client-side prediction, server reconciliation and snapshot interpolation. Built with Claude Code.
highlights: Measured 0.302 units median prediction error at 20% packet loss, and 2 corrections in 79 seconds on a home network. Up to 4 players, host over Unity Relay.

projects.name: Rollgeon
projects.description: Roguelike dice builder where your deck is a bag of dice and combat is based on Generala. In development.
roles: Mobile port and gamepad support, in collaboration with members of 3AM Games
highlights: Porting the game to mobile and adding controller support.

projects.name: SPCA x SOLAR
projects.description: Time-limited cat-rescue campaign game with SPCA, an animal rescue in Singapore. The campaign has ended.
highlights: Delivered within a fixed campaign window, with a mock layer so the game never waited on the backend.

projects.name: Unity Tools
projects.description: Five Unity editor tools published as UPM packages: Asset Renamer, PlayerPrefs Manager, Prefab Replacer, Project Zipper and Rename Items.
highlights: The Asset Renamer runs in SOLAR, a shipped commercial game.

projects.name: You Can't Always Push the Red Button
projects.description: Decision-making game for the Unity BA Game Jam 2026: you rule a cat nation and try not to just push the button. Made with Claude Code in 3 days.
roles: Programming, shared with Ignacio Martinez, 3-person team
highlights: Playable WebGL build on itch.io; decision system co-designed and balanced with Ignacio.

projects.name: Indie Community Bot
projects.description: Reusable Discord bot for indie game communities: welcome cards, devlogs, build notifications from CI and bug reports as private threads. All settings live per server in the database.
highlights: Running on Rollgeon's community server.

projects.name: Brain App
projects.description: Local-first AI assistant where the LLM never decides an action: it classifies intent, and deterministic code does the work. Private repository.
highlights: 323 test cases that run green in 77 seconds, 17 architecture decisions, 54 endpoints.
